results.reason: The response never identifies the Change of Control consent requirement in Section 15.4 that Varga's stock purchase triggers. It also never flags that Disclosure Schedule Part 3.5 wrongly treats the Crestline agreement as notice-only. Open Point B covers a change of control of Crestline, not of Halvorsen.

Issue 2 explains that §14.2, read with the §1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition, allows assignment without consent to any distributor in the Territory. It notes the definition does not exclude competitors or their affiliates.

Issue 1 explains that First Amendment §3.1 restates §12.3 so that only §9 breaches are carved out, dropping the §10 and §11 carve-outs. It says §17.5 precedence means the amendment controls, so Crestline's IP breaches and indemnity are now capped.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded 'breaches of Sections 9 and 10, and indemnification obligations under Section 11.'
The response states that the §12.2 cap is 'the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.'
The response is a memo with separate issues. Each issue gives the Document/Section, a 'Why it matters for Halvorsen' section, and a Recommended fix.
The response does not conclude that the Varga acquisition requires only notice to Crestline, or that no consent is needed. It simply does not address the point.
The response concludes the opposite: the IP and indemnity carve-outs were removed and those claims are now capped.
